title: Stability Gate: guided apply/rollback + perceptual evals for batching & cache tuning
creator: Aisha Coltrane
description: Build a lightweight acceptance harness and guided apply/rollback flow that ties automated batching/caching recommendations to perceptual quality checks. This ticket implements the runtime-side gate that will: evaluate candidate batching/cache configs on a small rolling population, run golden-prompt/perf regressions and aggregated perceptual metrics, and either commit the change or perform an automated rollback with incident metadata. The goal is to reduce token cost via safe autotuning without increasing user-visible quality regressions.
background: We have several autotune initiatives that recommend batching and KV-cache changes to reduce per-token cost. Previously, applying those changes caused subtle regressions in output fidelity for some workloads. Existing tickets created eval harnesses (golden prompts, sentinel suites) but there is no unified apply/rollback flow integrated with the runtime to run them automatically on candidate configs. This work fills that gap and provides an operator-friendly visibility surface for risky applies.
goals: Prototype an acceptance harness that runs a targeted eval suite (golden prompts + perceptual metrics) during a limited rollout
Create a guided apply/rollback workflow in the operator console with clear rationale and playbook steps
Automate rollback when quality thresholds are violated and surface artifact links and diffs in the incident record
Ensure telemetry for cost delta, latency delta, and quality metrics are stored and queryable by release/rollout
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can accept a candidate batching/cache config and orchestrate a 10% canary on a selected backend pool
Canary runs the configured golden-prompt suite and returns pass/fail based on configurable thresholds
If threshold is exceeded, system triggers an automated rollback and creates an incident with linked artifacts
Operator console shows per-route cost delta, latency impact, and a summary of failed golden prompts with text diffs
End-to-end test coverage for the apply/rollback flow and mocks for the golden-prompt oracle
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Integration tests on staging runtime with synthetic traffic (1 week)
Phase 1: Disable auto-commit. Expose guided-apply UI to SREs and PMs for manual approval (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Limited auto-commit for low-risk routes (e.g., internal diagnostics) with auto-rollback enabled (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Wider rollout with automated rollback and observability for customer-facing routes (gradual)
testing_plan: Unit tests for harness orchestration and acceptance decision logic
Integration tests: end-to-end apply -> canary -> eval -> commit/rollback on staging
Regression tests: inject known-good/known-bad model outputs to validate oracle sensitivity
Load tests: ensure canary harness does not introduce token bursts or KV-cache thrashing
metrics_to_monitor: per-prompt perplexity / edit-distance / BLEU-like perceptual metric
false_positive_rate of oracle (golden prompts that flagged acceptable changes)
risk_assessment: Medium. The main risk is spurious rollbacks due to an over-sensitive oracle which could prevent safe cost savings. Another risk is creating transient load patterns during canary that stress KV cache eviction. Mitigations: conservative initial thresholds, manual approval gate, and circuit-breaker on rollback frequency.
